display.title: Episode 519: The Big Barrel of Wine (Shabbos Zachor)
display.summary_short: Before Shabbos Zachor, Uncle Yossi explains why we remember Amalek, three young siblings say the Shema and two of the Twelve Pesukim, and the winemakers of Grape Town learn a costly lesson.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Parshas Zachor. Uncle Yossi explains the three verses everyone, young and old, must hear in shul: Amalek alone dared to attack the Jewish people after the Exodus, Haman was his descendant, and in every generation Hashem saves us from those who try to harm us. Mordechai gathered 22,000 children to learn Torah, and their pure voices brought Haman's downfall; today, too, children's Torah and mitzvos will bring Moshiach. He reminds soldiers of Tzivos Hashem to carry out the missions in their Purim newsletter, then leads the Hakochainik march. Three siblings, brought by their father, recite the Shema in Studio 604, and the younger two say verses from the Twelve Pesukim. After tzedakah comes the story of Grape Town, famous for its wine. To welcome the king, every resident must pour a gallon of wine into a giant barrel, but each one secretly pours water, thinking nobody will notice. When the king turns the golden faucet, out comes plain water. The show ends with Shabbos candle times and a reminder to hear Parshas Zachor.
display.lesson: If there is something good to do, do it yourself; never say 'let someone else do it', and set a good example for others.
